name: Vansen SyncPulse Haptic Interface Glove
description:
Slim-profile gloves in charcoal stretch-neoprene with embedded haptic actuator nodes at each fingertip and across the palm grid. Thin silver conductive traces are visible through the semi-translucent neoprene like circuit diagrams. Fingertips of the index and middle fingers on both hands are open-cut with conductive trim rings for direct augment-digit contact.

Designed to bridge organic and chrome hands simultaneously — the palm grid reads BCI signals and translates them into precise haptic feedback for remote manipulation, surgical assist, or AR interface use. Ships with a calibration dongle that clips to the wrist strap.
functionality: Haptic actuators provide tactile feedback in AR/VR environments and for remote robotic manipulation. Open-cut conductive fingertips allow direct chrome-digit BCI handshake. Palm grid reads passive BCI output. Calibration dongle syncs to most commercial neural port standards.
what_it_says: Precision work at the boundary of organic and machine — someone who earns through interface mastery.
story_hooks: A counterfeit batch of SyncPulse gloves has been traced to a Shelf workshop — they work fine but log all haptic input to an unknown server.
A remote surgeon relies on these gloves for operations across the city; when they malfunction mid-procedure, someone has to make a choice.
The calibration dongle format is compatible with a decommissioned military drone protocol — someone's been using consumer gloves to fly something they shouldn't.

physical_description.visual_profile: Second-skin gloves that blur the line between fashion and functional augmentation. The charcoal base creates a sleek, almost liquid appearance, while the visible silver conductive traces read as deliberate design—circuit diagrams mapped across the hand like a technical blueprint. Fingertip cutouts on index and middle fingers expose metallic conductive rings, suggesting direct neural integration. The overall effect is forensic precision meets street-tech utility.
physical_description.fit: Compression-fit through the palm and wrist, with articulated finger zones that allow full dexterity. The stretch-neoprene hugs the hand like a second skin without restricting movement. Wrist strap is snug but not tourniquet-tight—designed for all-day wear without circulation compromise.
physical_description.primary_material: Charcoal stretch-neoprene with embedded silicone haptic actuator nodes and silver conductive-trace threading
physical_description.texture: Smooth and slightly tacky to the touch—neoprene gives a moisture-resistant, grippy feel. The silver traces create fine linear ridges that catch light. Fingertip rings have a cool metallic smoothness, slightly raised at the edges.
physical_description.color_scheme: Charcoal gray base with silver-white conductive traces forming grid and circuit patterns. The traces are semi-translucent against the neoprene, creating depth and luminescence in dim light. Conductive trim rings at fingertips have a brushed-chrome finish.
physical_description.closures: Friction-fit wrist strap with integrated dongle clip; no traditional closures—the glove rolls onto the hand
distinctive_features: Visible haptic actuator nodes at each fingertip and distributed across palm grid
Open-cut fingertip design on index and middle fingers of both hands
Silver conductive traces visible through semi-translucent neoprene
BCI-to-haptic signal translation capability indicated by design
Vansen Systems branding embossed on inner wrist
physical_description.tier_indicator: Tier 1-2 luxury augmentation tech—expensive, cutting-edge, corporate-adjacent
physical_description.cultural_context: Corpo surgeon, remote-ops specialist, high-end AR interface user, or someone with significant chrome augmentation who needs a bridge between organic and synthetic sensory feedback. Signals wealth, technical sophistication, and deep integration with neural implants.
physical_description.condition_typical: Pristine or very lightly worn—these gloves are maintained like precision instruments. Any wear would be minor discoloration on the palm grid from frequent contact, never torn or patched.
